role.altitude: The geodetic surveyor keeps judging data quality, deciding which observations to reject, resolving database conflicts and directing field staff; computing closures in spreadsheets, copying coordinates into databases, typing station descriptions and phoning for progress shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining import scripts and validation rules
role.ambitious_version: A surveyor whose adjustments, accuracy statistics and database updates run on import, leaving the time for judging the network.

tasks.short: Compile accuracy statistics from the adjusted network, compare them with tolerances, analyze control or survey data for adherence to project specifications or land survey standards, and document the outcome.

steps.what: Surveyor compiles accuracy statistics per point from the adjusted survey data
Surveyor compares results with project specifications and survey standard tolerances
Surveyor analyzes whether the control or survey data adhere to standards and where problems lie

tasks.design: The adjustment software writes accuracy statistics per point and compares them with the project's tolerance profile in its report, instead of the surveyor copying results into a spreadsheet and checking each value. Analysing whether the data meet the standard stays with the surveyor. Writing up belongs to the technical reports task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Statistics were recomputed and checked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Adjustment software with accuracy reports and tolerance profiles.
tasks.still_hard: Projects with unusual or mixed specifications.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a pattern of small residuals points to a setup error.

reach.learn: Whether accepted control is ready sooner.

evidence.claim: Survey software runs least-squares adjustment, helps correct field blunders and writes adjustment reports.

assumptions: Boundary: analysing data against specifications; verifying new data (task 16292), assessing the need for more data (task 16300) and preparing reports (task 16294) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of preparing technical reports, which sibling task 16294 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: the adjusted network from task 16292 and a tolerance profile per project set up by the surveyor.
unknowns: Number of distinct specifications in use.

incremental.description: Surveyor sets up tolerance profiles for new specifications.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many custom specifications without a tolerance profile, so statistics are still compiled (s1 keeps 60) and compared (s2 keeps 60) by hand (15.7); high: standard profiles reused (25.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Import new coordinates and adjustment results, update station descriptions and photos, record quality assurance data, and resolve conflicts to maintain databases of geodetic information.

steps.what: Surveyor imports new coordinates and adjustment results into the geodetic database
Field staff record station descriptions, mark condition and photos at each visit: in paper notes today, in the field app linked to the station after the change
Surveyor updates descriptive data: station descriptions, mark condition and photos
Surveyor records quality assurance data: accuracy, method and date
Surveyor checks consistency and resolves duplicate or conflicting records

tasks.design: An import script takes coordinates and accuracy figures straight from the adjustment export, checks datum, epoch and point identifiers, and writes quality data with method and date, instead of copying values by hand. Field staff capture station descriptions, mark condition and photos in a field app linked to the station, and the surveyor checks them rather than typing up notes. Resolving duplicates and conflicts stays with the surveyor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordinates and descriptions were copied by hand between files.
tasks.enabler_now: Adjustment exports, import scripts and field apps linked to the database.
tasks.still_hard: Old stations with conflicting historical coordinates.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which of two coordinates for an old mark to trust.

reach.role: data user at a government agency
reach.learn: Whether published data are current and complete.

evidence.claim: Survey software writes adjustment reports that can be exported.
Databases, verification and distribution of survey data work deterministically with adjustment and QA rules.

assumptions: Boundary: maintaining the database; distributing data (task 16290) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1 and s3: adjustment exports from task 16292.
Input contract for s2: field staff use the field app for about 70% of station visits (s5, share 1); s2 is priced at that share.
Resolving conflicts keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of legacy stations with conflicts.
research_questions: Do database errors reported by users fall?

incremental.description: Surveyor maintains the import script and validation rules.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many legacy records and paper notes, so imports need hand fixes (s1 keeps 60) and notes are still typed (s2 keeps 80) (30.1); high: new networks with field app capture (46.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Import raw observations, run closures and least-squares adjustment, decide on flagged blunders to verify the mathematical correctness of newly collected survey data, and record the verification.

steps.what: Surveyor imports raw observations from receivers and instruments
Surveyor computes loop closures and runs the least-squares adjustment to verify the mathematical correctness
Surveyor decides which flagged observations are blunders and removes or keeps them

tasks.design: Raw observations are imported directly from receivers and total stations in their native formats. The adjustment software computes loop closures, runs the least-squares adjustment and flags observations that fail the outlier tests, instead of closures worked out in spreadsheets. The surveyor decides on each flagged observation. Recording the result belongs to the database and report tasks and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closures and checks were computed in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Adjustment software with outlier tests and direct instrument import.
tasks.still_hard: Networks mixing old and new observation types.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing from the field notes which setup was disturbed.

ambition.what: Verify data each field day instead of at the end of the campaign.

tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic; deciding on blunders stays.

reach.learn: Whether re-observations are requested while still on site.

evidence.claim: Survey software runs least-squares adjustment and helps correct field blunders.

assumptions: Boundary: verifying new data; requesting additional data (task 16293) and maintaining the database (task 16295) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of maintaining quality assurance data, which sibling task 16295 covers; its saving is counted there.
Deciding on blunders keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of instruments with direct import.
research_questions: Are blunders caught before field staff leave the site?

incremental.description: Surveyor maintains import formats and outlier test settings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mixed legacy observations that need conversion, so s1 keeps 80 and closures are partly still worked out by hand, so s2 keeps 60 (16.5); high: modern instruments with direct import (33.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan field campaigns and assign staff and equipment, brief staff on methods, provide technical consultation, and track campaign progress to plan or direct the work of geodetic surveying staff.

steps.what: Surveyor plans field campaigns: staff, equipment and sites, in a spreadsheet rebuilt each time today, on the planning board after the change
Surveyor checks the final campaign plan: each person's sites, dates, equipment and qualifications
Surveyor publishes the checked assignments to the surveying staff on the board
Surveyor briefs surveying staff on methods and specifications
Surveyor provides technical consultation to staff during the work

tasks.design: Field campaigns are planned on a board showing staff qualifications, equipment availability and site access windows, instead of a spreadsheet rebuilt for each campaign. Briefing and technical consultation stay personal. Progress per campaign comes from observation uploads, so the surveyor sees which stations are done without phoning around. Progress is shown per campaign, not per person; any per-person view is agreed with the works council first.

approvals.approved_version: The campaign assignments with each person's sites, dates and equipment exactly as checked by the surveyor in s1b, published once to the assigned staff on the planning board; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Plans lived in spreadsheets and progress came by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Planning boards and upload-based progress views.
tasks.still_hard: Weather and access changes on the day.
tasks.human_edge: Solving a field problem over the phone from experience.

reach.learn: Whether plans change less on the day.

evidence.claim: Tools that log staff work need works council consent.
No AI Act high-risk area covers surveying; planning by qualifications is rule-based.

assumptions: Boundary: planning and directing staff; training in observation methods (task 16288) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: observation uploads from task 16292 imports.
Briefing and consultation keep their full time.
research_questions: Do campaigns finish on schedule more often?

incremental.description: Surveyor keeps qualifications and equipment on the board current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one campaign at a time, so the board saves little planning (s1 keeps 85) and uploads lag, so phoning stays (s4 keeps 75) (7.6); high: several parallel campaigns as designed (15.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
